DecSummary: The worker suffered a minor low back strain in 1987.  The employer appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer granting only 50% SIEF relief.

The worker suffered a low back injury from lifting in April 1992.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for cervical disability which the worker claimed resulted from physiotherapy in May 1993 for the compensable injury.

The worker suffered a compression fracture at T12 and a crack fracture at L2 when he fell a distance of 12 feet in 1969.  The Board granted a 5% pension effective in 1985 with an increase to 10% in 1993.  The worker appealed the retroactivity date and the amount of the pension.
The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a herniated disc.

The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer which granted increases in her pensions for low back disability from 10% to 15% and her neck disability from 15% to 20% but denied a pension for shoulder disability.

DecKeywords: Benefit of the doubt; Permanent disability
DecSummary: The worker fractured his arm in February 1989.  He returned to modified work in June 1989 but strained his arm two weeks later.  The strain was found to be an aggravation of the earlier arm injury.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying a pension for permanent disability.

DecKeywords: Future economic loss {FEL} (deemed earnings); Temporary total disability
DecSummary: A cleaner suffered a finger injury in 1991.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying temporary total disability benefits from September 1993 to December 1993, and denying a FEL award in December 1993.

A 15-year-old student in 1991 with a summer job suffered massive trauma to his lower extremities when he was caught in a cement mixer.  In determining the earnings basis for the worker's FEL award, the Board based his benefits on the average industrial wage for 1991.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer regarding the earnings basis.

DecKeywords: Board Directives and Guidelines (interest); Interest (employer assessment)
DecSummary: The Board granted a retroactive reclassification of the employer for the years 1986-1992.  The employer appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying interest.

DecKeywords: Earnings basis (learner); Supplements, transitional provisions (permanent) (wage loss)
DecSummary: The worker suffered accidents in 1967, 1986, 1987 and 1988.  The worker appealed a decision of the Reinstatement Officer denying supplementary benefits under s. 147(4) of the pre-1997 Act.

The worker suffered a low back injury in 1985 for which she was granted a 10% pension.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying supplementary benefits under s. 147(4) of the pre-1997 Act after 1994 and denying entitlement for chronic pain.

The worker suffered an arm injury in 1992.  In 1994, he was granted a FEL sustainability award.  The employer appealed a decision of the Mediation Officer confirming the sustainability award and refusing to remove the projected FEL costs from the employer's NEER calculation.  In Decision No. 773/97I, a different panel confirmed the FEL sustainability award.
The worker appealed and the employer cross-appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer which increased the worker's NEL award from 14% to 29%.
The application under s. 17(2) of the pre-1997 Act was withdrawn as the matter had been settled.  [3 pages]

The worker's application to reconsider Decision No. 516/97 was denied.  The fact that there was a dissenting opinion in Decision No. 516/97 did not, in itself, give grounds for reconsideration.  [3 pages]

DecKeywords: Earnings basis (apprentice); Earnings basis (seasonal employment); Reconsideration (advisability) (finality); Reconsideration (error of law)
DecSummary: The employer applied to reconsider Decision No. 486/97I.

The worker fell down some stairs in December 1992 and received benefits until May 1993.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for a neck and head injury, denying entitlement for chronic pain and denying benefits after May 1993.

The worker suffered a low back strain in 1979 while he was helping a co-worker climb out of a pit.  The worker also suffered back injuries in June 1983 and March 1987.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying temporary benefits in November 1987 and denying a pension for permanent disability.
The worker was injured in November 1990.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying a NEL award.

The worker suffered a hand injury in 1980 for which she was granted a 7% pension.  In 1987, she was also granted a 10% provisional pension for psychiatric disability.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying a permanent pension for psychiatric disability.

DecKeywords: Adjournment (referral to Board); Investigation by Tribunal (cooperation)
DecSummary: A self-employed worker with personal coverage appealed decisions of the Board regarding the earnings basis for benefits and VR services.
The worker suffered low back strains in 1990 and 1991.  The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting entitlement for chronic pain.

DecKeywords: Jurisdiction, Tribunal (final decision of Board); Reconsideration (issue setting); Reconsideration (jurisdiction)
DecSummary: The employer applied to reconsider Decision No. 304/97.  The worker had appealed a decision of the Board finding that the worker refused suitable employment.  The hearing panel obtained a report from a Tribunal medical assessor.  The assessor concluded that the worker was suffering from chronic pain.  The hearing panel then concluded that the worker had entitlement for chronic pain.  Considering the chronic pain, the hearing panel concluded that the work offered by the employer was not suitable.

The Board granted the employer 75% SIEF relief for an accident.  It correctly processed the SIEF relief for temporary benefits but did not process the SIEF relief on the worker's NEL award.  The Board then granted a retroactive adjustment of the employer's NEER account to reflect the SIEF relief on the NEL award.  The employer appealed a decision of the Experience Rating Officer denying interest on the retroactive adjustment.
The worker's application to reconsider Decision No. 1151/97 was denied.  The worker was essentially attempting to re-argue the case.  [5 pages]

DecKeywords: Apportionment (negligence); Experience rating (NEER) (retroactive adjustment); Transfer of costs (NEER)
DecSummary: The worker was injured in March 1992 while employed by another employer.  In September 1992, the costs of the claim were transferred to the employer under s. 10(9) of the pre-1997 Act.  The employer objected, and in February 1994, the Board confirmed the decision to transfer the costs to the employer.  The employer appealed to the Hearings Officer.  In November 1995, the Hearings Officer again confirmed the Board decision.  From the worker's testimony at the Hearings Officer hearing, the employer learned about a previous accident.  The employer applied for SIEF relief, and in February 1996, the Board granted 50% SIEF relief.  The employer then applied for retroactive adjustment of its NEER account to reflect the SIEF relief.  The employer appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying the retroactive adjustment.

DecKeywords: Benefit of the doubt; Cancer (lung); Smoking
DecSummary: The worker's widow appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying the worker entitlement for lung cancer.

The worker suffered a low back injury in 1992 for which he was granted a 1% NEL award.  This was increased to 6% by the Senior NEL Adjudicator.  The worker appealed denial of a further increase in the NEL award.

DecKeywords: Benefit of the doubt; Hearing loss (flat audiometric curve)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for hearing loss.

DecKeywords: In the course of employment (reasonably incidental activity test); Right to sue (remoteness)
DecSummary: The plaintiff in a court action worked for the defendant as an automobile mechanic.  He was injured when he slipped and fell on ice in the defendant's employee parking lot.

The worker suffered shoulder, neck and back injuries in July 1991, for which she was granted a 29% NEL award.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for a recurrence in August 1994.

The worker suffered a back injury in January 1989.  He returned to work in April 1989 but stopped working in August 1989.  He returned to work again in November 1989 but stopped working again due to a recurrence in April 1990.  After the recurrence in November 1989, he received temporary total disability benefits until March 1991.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer granting only 50% temporary partial disability benefits from March 1991 until he was granted a 20% pension in December 1991.

The worker suffered facial lacerations, trauma to his face and loss of four front lower teeth in a compensable accident.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for treatment for his upper teeth.
The worker appealed a decision of the Reinstatement Officer denying supplementary benefits under s. 43(9) of the pre-1997 Act from February 1996 to October 1996.

DecKeywords: Adjournment (peremptory hearing date); Three week rule (documents)
DecSummary: The original hearing of the worker's appeal was adjourned to obtain additional medical evidence.  Less than three weeks prior to the reconvened hearing, the worker sent three additional medical reports.

The employer appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer granting benefits for a recurrence.  The hearing was adjourned sine die to allow the employer to return to the Board for a final decision on entitlement for a number of other recurrences, which the employer also wanted to appeal.  [4 pages]

The worker requested clarification of Decision No. 303/97, in which the hearing panel found that the worker was entitled to full benefits during a specific period.  The worker submitted that the Board had not properly implemented the decision because it reduced the worker's benefits.

DecKeywords: Causation (thin skull doctrine) (psychotraumatic disability); Psychotraumatic disability (no physical injury); Significant contribution (of compensable accident to psychological condition); Stress, mental
DecSummary: The worker had been working for the accident employer for 32 years.  In 1987, he reported to Supervisor A who reported to Supervisor B.  Neither supervisor wanted the worker to copy Supervisor B on memos the worker was sending to Supervisor A.  In February 1987, Supervisor A had a discussion with the worker about the worker copying memos to Supervisor B.  The worker was taken to hospital after this discussion and released the same day.  He did not return to work.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for psychotraumatic disability.

A health care aide suffered a low back injury in October 1990.  The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer finding that work offered by the employer in December 1992 was not suitable or comparable to the worker's pre-injury job.

The worker's application to reconsider Decision No. 373/97 was denied.  In Decision No. 373/97, the hearing panel confirmed the Board's decision regarding the worker's FEL award based on deemed earnings in appropriate work.  The worker submitted that he had a herniated disc and was unable to work.  The hearing panel considered the evidence and came to a reasonable conclusion.  It was uncertain that the worker suffered a herniated disc and, even if he did, the preponderance of evidence established that he was not totally disabled.  [5 pages]

DecKeywords: Chronic obstructive lung disease; Exposure (silica dust); Smoking
DecSummary: The worker worked at a plant that produced graphite electrodes from 1965 to 1992.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for chronic obstructive lung disease, diagnosed in 1993.

A sewing machine operator experienced left shoulder pain in February 1990.  She stopped working in February 1992.  In May 1993, she was granted a zero FEL award.  In April 1994, she was granted a 26% NEL award.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying temporary benefits after October 1992 and denying entitlement for fibromyalgia.

The worker applied to reconsider Decision No. 1337/97 on the basis of new evidence.  In Decision No. 1337/97R, the Panel noted that the new evidence was illegible, and allowed the worker until a specific date to obtain a transcription of the evidence, failing which the application to reconsider would be denied.  The worker now applied to extend the date since the doctor whose notes had to be transcribed was apparently indisposed.

DecKeywords: Psychotraumatic disability; Pensions (reassessment); Supplements, temporary; Supplements, transitional provisions (permanent)
DecSummary: A farm worker suffered a low back injury while throwing bales of hay in 1969.  He underwent surgery in 1970 and 1971.  He was granted a 20% pension for low back disability.  The worker also suffered a torn mensicus when he stepped down from a truck in 1981.  He was granted a 15% pension for knee disability.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying an increase in the pensions, denying entitlement for psychotraumatic disability and denying supplementary benefits.

DecKeywords: Earnings basis (deemed worker); Earnings basis (truck driver); Personal coverage (actual earnings)
DecSummary: A self-employed truck driver with personal coverage was injured in 1992.  The worker had personal coverage at the statutory maximum of $50,800.  The Board originally based benefits on the statutory maximum.  Later, the Board looked at financial records and found that the worker had gross income in 1992 of about $60,000.  The Board then presumed that net earnings a truck driver were one-third of gross earnings, and based benefits on net earnings of about $20,000.  In addition, for 1993, the Board made a further reduction based on its findings of the amount of lost business suffered by the worker in 1993.  The worker appealed.

The worker suffered a right knee injury in 1967.  He underwent a number of surgeries including a total replacement in 1992 and a revision in 1993.  He was granted a 3% pension in 1976, increased over the years to 35% in 1991 but reduced to 20% in 1993.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying an increase in the pension and denying further temporary benefits in 1993.
The worker suffered a low back injury in November 1991.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying ongoing entitlement.

DecKeywords: Second Injury and Enhancement Fund {SIEF} (preexisting condition)
DecSummary: The worker suffered from right epicondylitis and right deQuervain's tenosynovitis in June 1993.  In January 1994, a right anterior shoulder subluxation was diagnosed, but was found not to be compensable.  The employer claimed that the shoulder condition was a preexisting condition which prolonged or enhanced the worker's disability.  The employer appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying SIEF relief.

DecKeywords: Obesity; Second Injury and Enhancement Fund {SIEF} (preexisting condition)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a low back strain in 1992.  The employer appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying SIEF relief.

The worker suffered a back injury in 1986.  In June 1989, the Board recognized entitlement for hip disability.  The Board granted 50% SIEF relief for temporary benefits.  In 1996, the Board increased the SIEF relief to 90%.  The employer appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying retroactive adjustment of the employer's NEER account to reflect the increased SIEF relief.

The worker suffered a back injury in 1989.  The employer was granted 50% SIEF relief in 1996.  The employer appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying retroactive adjustment of the employer's NEER account to reflect the SIEF relief.

The worker suffered a shoulder injury in 1991, diagnosed as rotator cuff tendonitis.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for thoracic outlet syndrome and reflex sympathetic dystrophy, diagnosed in 1994.

The worker suffered a back and neck injury in 1982 for which he was granted a 20% pension.  He suffered an aggravation in May 1995 and was granted temporary total disability benefits from May 1995 to December 1995.  The worker appealed a decision of the Dispute Resolution Officer denying temporary total disability benefits from December 1995 to August 1996.
The worker's appeal was withdrawn at the request of the worker.  [2 pages]
The worker worked in various mills and mines from 1977 to 1993.  The worker's widow appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for the worker's death from sarcoidosis.

At the end of the first day of the hearing of the worker's appeal, the hearing was adjourned to obtain further evidence.  At the reconvened hearing, the employer was represented by a different representative working for the same company as represented the employer on the first day of hearing.  This new representative was not familiar with the proceedings on the first day of the hearing and was not prepared.

The worker suffered a low back injury when he slipped in August 1969.  He returned to work four days later.  The worker underwent back surgery in 1981.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for the surgery.

DecKeywords: Board Directives and Guidelines (penalty assessments) (time limits); Reconsideration (new evidence)
DecSummary: The employer's application to reconsider Decision No. 1692/97 was denied.  The employer had missed the Board's cut-off date for appealing a penalty assessment.  The hearing panel found a lack of due diligence by the employer.  The employer submitted new evidence that it had requested information from the Board but did not receive it until five days before the cut-off date, making compliance impossible.  The Vice-Chair found that there was a lack of due diligence by the employer.  The Board took six weeks to respond to the employer's request for information.  Delay was much more the responsibility of the employer than the Board.  [4 pages]

DecKeywords: Permanent impairment {NEL} (redetermination) (unanticipated deterioration); Temporary disability (beyond pension level)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a knee injuries in October 1991 and June 1994, for which he was granted a 7% NEL award.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying benefits for a recurrence in November 1995 and denying a reassessment of the NEL award.

DecKeywords: Causation (thin skull doctrine) (psychotraumatic disability); Psychotraumatic disability
DecSummary: The worker suffered a low back injury from lifting in May 1991.  He was granted a 20% NEL award for chronic pain.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for psychotraumatic disability.

DecKeywords: Adjournment (referral to Board); Hemorrhage (subarachnoid); Psychotraumatic disability
DecSummary: The worker injured her coccyx in a fall in January 1993, for which she was granted a 17% NEL award.  She suffered a subarachnoid hemorrhage in a fall at home in April 1994.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying ongoing benefits after April 1994, denying entitlement for the subarachnoid hemorrhage, denying initial entitlement for cervical pain and depression and denying an increase in the worker's FEL award.

The worker experienced shoulder and neck pain in 1977 after lifting and moving heavy material.  He was granted a 5% pension for shoulder disability, increased to 10% in 1996, retroactive to 1995.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying a pension for neck disability, denying entitlement for chronic pain or psychotraumatic disability, denying supplementary benefits prior to January 1992 and denying further arrears of the pension increase.
The worker appealed a decision of the Dispute Resolution Officer denying entitlement for a shoulder injury the worker claimed he suffered in 1995 when he was struck on the shoulder.
The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying an increase in the worker's pension.

DecKeywords: Future economic loss {FEL} (deemed earnings); Jurisdiction, Tribunal (final decision of Board)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a back injury in July 1992.  The Board granted benefits until January 1993, when it found that the worker refused suitable employment.  The Board also found that there was no evidence of permanent impairment and, consequently, a FEL assessment was not performed.  The worker appealed a decision of the Reinstatement Officer finding that the work offered in January 1993 was suitable and denying temporary benefits after January 1993.

The employer applied to reconsider Decision No. 1476/97 in which the hearing panel concluded that the costs of an accident which occurred while a worker was travelling to a work site were correctly included in the employer's CAD-7 experience rating account.  The employer submitted that the hearing panel fettered its discretion by failing to consider the merits and justice of the case and that it failed to apply Tribunal precedent.

The worker suffered head, shoulder, neck and rib injuries when he fell 12 feet in May 1990.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for chronic pain, memory loss, depression and low back disability.
The worker applied to reconsider Decision No. 1063/97.  The worker submitted that the hearing panel failed to make a determination on the issue of whether the worker had entitlement for chronic pain.

The employer applied to reconsider Decision No. 974/97.  The employer submitted that there was an error of law by the hearing panel, in that its findings of fact were inconsistent with its conclusion.

DecKeywords: Suitable employment; Transfer of costs (Schedule 2 employer)
DecSummary: An airline worker suffered a back injury in January 1992.  He returned to work with restrictions in February 1992 but stopped working after a few days due to a recurrence.  In May 1993, a Board claims adjudicator found that the worker could return to modified work that did not involve excessive lifting or pushing.  The employer offered such work but it was refused by the worker.  The worker's benefits were terminated and his VR file was closed.  On appeal, the Reinstatement Officer found that the work offered by the employer was not suitable, and granted the worker additional VR assistance and full benefits from May 1993 until completion of the program.  The employer appealed.

The worker suffered back and shoulder strain in a fall from a stepladder in January 1988.  He received benefits until November 1989.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying a pension for permanent disability.
The worker withdrew his appeal after being advised of possible downside risk of pursuing the claim.  [3 pages]
The worker worked as a shipwright in Ontario from 1971 to 1987.  He died in 1988 from mesothelioma.  The worker's widow appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying dependency benefits.

The worker's application to reconsider Decision No. 668/97 was denied.  New evidence provided by the worker added nothing of substance to the understanding of the extent of the worker's disability.  However, the Vice-Chair recommended that the Board consider whether to forgive an overpayment.  [3 pages]

DecKeywords: Aggravation (preexisting condition) (hematoma); Apportionment (pensions) (co-existing conditions); Pensions (assessment) (cognitive impairment)
DecSummary: The worker and employer appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer confirming a 50% pension.

The worker was injured in 1986.  In 1987, the Board granted the employer 50% SIEF relief.  In 1988, the Board granted the worker a 10% pension but, through clerical oversight, neglected to apply the SIEF relief to the pension, until the employer brought the oversight to the Board's attention in 1995.  The Board made a retroactive adjustment to the employer's NEER account, resulting in a refund of about $18,000.  The employer appealed a decision of the Board denying interest on the refund.

The worker suffered a low back strain in January 1991, for which she was granted a 5% NEL award.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for chronic pain and denying supplementary benefits under s. 43(9) of the pre-1997 Act after May 1994.

The worker suffered a low back strain and whiplash in a compensable motor vehicle accident in November 1993.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for a recurrence in January 1995.

A police constable suffered shoulder and neck strain and chest discomfort after he tried to break down a door in May 1976.  He returned to work after about one week.  He was also granted benefits for two short recurrences in 1979.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying ongoing benefits for his condition and denying entitlement for addiction to painkillers.

The worker suffered a repetitive strain injury in 1991.  The employer placed the worker on a temporary modified work program, so that the worker did not lose any time.  In January 1994, the employer stated that it could not continue providing the modified duties, and terminated the worker's employment.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying lost time benefits.

DecKeywords: Second Injury and Enhancement Fund {SIEF} (preexisting condition); Second Injury and Enhancement Fund {SIEF} (prolonged disability)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a rotator cuff tear while pulling a heavy skid.  The employer appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying SIEF relief.

The worker's application to reconsider Decision No. 848/97 was denied.  The worker submitted that he was poorly advised by his representative.  The Vice-Chair stated that the worker could pursue a remedy against his representative through other forums, not through the Tribunal.  [3 pages]

The worker suffered neck and low back injuries in a compensable motor vehicle accident in 1987.  The employer appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer granting pensions for headaches and neck disability.
The worker's application to reconsider Decision No. 1060/97 was denied.  The hearing panel considered the evidence and came to a reasonable conclusion.  [4 pages]

The worker was struck on the ankle in 1961.  He sustained a small laceration which later became a chronic infection and developed into phlebitis.  He was left with post-phlebitis syndrome.  The worker was granted a 7% pension in 1964, increased to 10% in 1968 and 15% in 1992.

DecKeywords: Arising out of employment; Heart attack; Presumptions (entitlement)
DecSummary: The worker's widow appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying dependency benefits for the worker's death from a heart attack.

DecKeywords: Commutation (business investment); Pensions (assessment) (back); Pensions (assessment) (knee); Supplements, transitional provisions (permanent)
DecSummary: The worker was injured in July 1979.  He was granted a 40% pension for low back disability, a 5% pension for thoracic back disability and a 7.5% pension for bilateral knee disability.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying commutation of the pension, denying an increase in the pension for thoracic back and knee disability and denying supplementary benefits under s. 147(4) of the pre-1997 Act.
The worker suffered a left knee injury in August 1991.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for left hip disability.

DecKeywords: Supplements, transitional provisions (permanent) (retirement); Supplements, transitional provisions (permanent) (wage loss)
DecSummary: A mine labourer suffered a back injury in 1956.  As a result of Board-sponsored on-the-job training, the worker became an insurance adjuster.  He later opened his own business.  He sold his business in 1986 and retired after advice from his doctor to slow down in order to avoid a heart attack.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying supplementary benefits under s. 147(4) of the pre-1997 Act.
The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for left knee disability which he related to compensable accidents in 1990 and 1991 and the nature of his employment.

The worker mixed and used various dyes.  In June 1992, he left work and went to the hospital due to dizziness and nausea.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer granting entitlement for only one day.
The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for right carpal tunnel syndrome.

The worker appealed a decision of the Dispute Resolution Officer denying commutation of the worker's 20% pension, valued at about $36,000, which the worker wanted to pay debts he incurred to pay legal fees for his children.
The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for right shoulder disability.
The worker suffered a back injury in 1991.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying further entitlement for periods in 1995 and 1996.

The worker suffered a low back injury in 1985 for which she was granted a 10% pension.  She suffered a further back injury in January 1993.  She returned to work in May 1993 but stopped working one week later.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer granting only 50% benefits for temporary partial disability from May 1993 to July 1994 and denying temporary benefits after September 1995.

DecKeywords: Chronic pain; Significant contribution (of compensable accident to disability)
DecSummary: A construction worker fell five feet from a ladder in 1981, suffering low back and head injuries.  He fell in 1986, injuring his knee.  He suffered a low back strain from lifting in September 1989.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying ongoing entitlement for the 1989 accident after January 1990 and denying entitlement for chronic pain.
A press operator suffered a crush injury in November 1993.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer basing benefits on the worker's earnings over the year prior to the accident.

DecKeywords: Adjournment (referral to Board); Permanent impairment {NEL} (rating schedule) (unlisted condition)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a  decision of the Senior NEL Adjudicator granting a 3% NEL award for a rib condition.

The worker fell from a ladder and struck his head in January 1991.  He continues to suffer from post-traumatic headaches.  The Board granted a full FEL award at D1 in August 1992 but reduced the FEL award to a sustainability award at R1 on the basis that the worker could return to his pre-accident job with accommodations.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer confirming the R1 FEL award.

The employer company was owned equally by a husband and wife.  The company appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer finding that the wife was not an executive officer of the company in 1991 and 1992 and, therefore, including her wages in the firm payroll.
The worker fractured her arm when she tripped and fell in July 1992.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying temporary benefits after July 1993.
The worker suffered from epicondylitis as a result of the repetitive nature of his work.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying a pension for permanent disability.

DecKeywords: Pensions (assessment) (chronic pain); Temporary disability (beyond pension level)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a back injury in 1987.  In 1991, he was granted a 25% pension for chronic pain.  In March 1993, he suffered a recurrence and received temporary benefits until May 1993.  In 1996, his chronic pain pension was increased to 30%.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying temporary benefits after May 1993 and denying a further increase in the pension.
The worker suffered a low back injury in November 1991.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying benefits after September 1992.
The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for asthma which he related to exposure to TDI while working for a manufacturer of foam products.

A health care aide suffered a thoracic and lumbar sprain while moving a patient in January 1988.  She was granted a 10% pension which was paid as a lump sum.  In 1991, the organic pension was replaced by a 15% pension for chronic pain.  The worker appealed decisions of the Board denying commutation of the remaining 5% of the pension, denying entitlement for headaches and irritable bowel and denying health care benefits for orthopaedic shoes, elbow splints and a cervical collar.
The worker's application to reconsider Decision No. 678/97 was denied.  The worker was essentially rearguing the position taken at the original hearing.

The worker was a heavy equipment operator.  On October 9, 1989, he slipped and fell on his machine.  In early November 1989, he received a jolt when the machine tipped up and then slammed down on the ground.  On November 17, 1989, he took a nap in the cab of his machine during lunch time and was unable to get up.  He was diagnosed with a burst fracture of the first lumbar vertebra.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for the burst fracture.

DecKeywords: Continuing entitlement; Future economic loss {FEL} (time periods) (occupational disease)
DecSummary: A waitress suffered a shoulder injury in September 1992.  She underwent surgery in November 1992 due to laxity in the shoulders, specifically multi-directional instability.  The worker was granted a 17% NEL award.  She was granted a FEL award as of October 1993.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting reduced temporary partial disability benefits from April 1993 to May 1993, denying temporary benefits after May 1993, confirming the NEL award and granting the FEL award as of October 1993.

The worker was injured in 1989.  In 1991, the Board granted 50% SIEF relief.  In 1992, the Board increased the SIEF relief to 75%.  That increase was reflected in the employer's VER experience rating account for 1991.  The employer appealed a decision of the Board denying retroactive adjustment of its account for the years 1989, 1990 and 1991.

The worker was a building manager at an egg hatchery.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for a respiratory condition that the worker claimed resulted from exposure to paraformaldehyde which was used to decontaminate the nests.
The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for carpal tunnel syndrome which the worker related to the nature of her work for a shoe manufacturer.

An ambulance attendant suffered a back injury when she slipped while carrying a stretcher in 1990.  She suffered further back problems in 1994 after moving piles of paper on her desk.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying a permanent impairment award.

DecKeywords: Jurisdiction, Tribunal (commencement of hearing); Pensions (assessment) (white finger disease); Rehabilitation, vocational (eligibility) (termination of employment)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer confirming a 2% pension for white finger disease and denying VR services and supplementary benefits after March 1993.
The worker suffered an upper back strain when he slipped as he was lifting an object.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for low back disability.

DecKeywords: Future economic loss {FEL} (deemed earnings); Permanent impairment {NEL} (degree of impairment) (chronic pain)
DecSummary: A sewing machine operator suffered a right shoulder injury in August 1990.  Originally, the Board granted a 28% NEL award and a zero FEL award.  In 1995, the Board allowed entitlement for chronic pain and granted a 15% NEL award, but the Board replaced the 28% NEL award with the 15% award.  As a result of a decision of the Reinstatement Officer, the worker's FEL award was reassessed.  The Board found that the worker could have returned to work as a sewing machine operator but at slightly reduced wages.  Accordingly, the Board granted a small FEL award.  The worker appealed regarding the NEL and FEL awards.
An office cleaner appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for varicose veins.

DecSummary: A wood cutter started working for the accident employer, a new company, in July 1993.  The worker was injured in January 1994. The worker objected, claiming that he was actually earning about $645 per week at the time of the accident.  The Board then recalculated benefits under s. 40(1)(b).  It found that the worker was only employed for nine weeks from July 1993 to January 1994, and earned just over $6,000.  It factored in the periods of unemployment as being characteristic of the employment cycle in the industry, and accordingly reduced the worker's earnings basis to $242 per week.  The worker appealed.

The Board forgave the overpayment for the years until 1991 but decided to collect the overpayment for the years from 1991 to 1994.  The worker appealed.

The worker appealed a decision of the Senior NEL Adjudicator granting a 15% NEL award for back disability.
The employer appealed a decision of the Decision Review Specialist denying interest on assessment adjustments.

The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for a left knee condition, denying a permanent impairment assessment and denying entitlement for chronic pain.

On application by the employer, the Board recalculated based on the worker's earnings during the year preceding the accident but not including unemployment insurance benefits.  The worker appealed.

DecKeywords: Second Injury and Enhancement Fund {SIEF} (preexisting condition)

DecKeywords: Second Injury and Enhancement Fund {SIEF} (preexisting condition)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a left chest wall injury, diagnosed as costochondritis.  The employer appealed a decision of the Dispute Resolution Officer denying SIEF relief.

DecKeywords: Administrative Fund (transfer of costs); Suitable employment
DecSummary: Five months after the worker's injury, the employer offered her modified janitorial work.  The Board telephoned the worker and told her to report to work that same night or her benefits would be terminated.  The Board also immediately cancelled a multi-disciplinary assessment for which it had approved the worker's registration.  The worker's initial reaction was that she could not perform any janitorial duties, but she reported to work that night.  The employer was given an intimidating letter to read and sign which established an inflexible approach by the employer.  No one was available from the employer to answer the worker's questions or concerns about the work.  The worker left the premises after one half hour without attempting the work.  The Board  terminated the worker's benefits the next day, based on information provided by the employer, without speaking to the worker.  The worker did not review the modified work duties with her doctor.

DecKeywords: Second Injury and Enhancement Fund {SIEF} (severity of preexisting condition)

DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying partial commutation of his pension, valued at about $38,000, in the amount of $21,000, for the purpose of paying off his mortgage.

The worker suffered a back injury in 1990.  In 1996, the employer was granted 50% SIEF relief.  The employer appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying retroactive adjustment of the employer's CAD-7 experience rating account to reflect the SIEF relief.

The Dispute Resolution Officer found that the chondromalacia was a major underlying preexisting condition.  The Dispute Resolution Officer did not grant SIEF relief at the time but stated that, if a permanent impairment develops, the employer will be entitled to 90% SIEF relief.  The employer appealed denial of SIEF relief.

In 1974, the worker injured his right hand when a heavy motor fell on his hand and wrist.  He had abrasions over the dorsum of the wrist and swelling and spasm.  He was diagnosed with a soft tissue injury, and provided with a cast which he wore for two weeks.  X-rays revealed no injury to the bones.  The worker returned to work after two weeks.  In 1991, the worker was diagnosed with carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) of the right hand.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Officer denying entitlement for CTS.

The worker injured his back in 1962 and was off work for eight days.  The Board originally denied entitlement and the worker did not pursue the matter further until 1991.  The Board then granted entitlement for the accident but denied any further entitlement.

The worker experienced a gradual onset of low back pain on May 10, 1994.  He continued to work at modified work until May 31, 1994.  The worker appealed denial of full temporary benefits after May 31, 1994, denial of entitlement for chronic pain and denial of a permanent impairment assessment.  The employer cross-appealed granting of 50% benefits from May 31, 1994, to September 1994.

This s. 17 application was withdrawn by the applicant upon settlement of the court action.  [3 pages]

The issues were overlapping.  Whether the worker is entitled to benefits for psychological disability as a result of the compensable injury will affect the determination as to the suitability of modified work.  [6 pages]
